title: Vanguard rollout rituals — field journal and handoff checklist
content:
Context and purpose:
This is my running log of the "vanguard" approach — a tiny, highly-observed cohort that we route through a new model version or config change before we do broader canaries. Goal: catch atypical failure modes (latency cliffs, degenerate outputs, client-specific regressions) while keeping blast radius tiny and operational overhead low.

Quick principles (mental model):
- Smaller than a canary: think 0.25% of traffic or 2–5 unique tenants, whichever is smaller.
- High-observability: add extra tracing, full responses sampled, and end-to-end client-level checks for those cohorts.
- Defined ritual: fixed warmup, escalating traffic, explicit go/no-go signals. Rituals reduce decision friction during off-hours.
- Safe defaults: circuit breaker at both sidecar and router, immediate pinback script ready.

Pre-vanguard checklist (before we flip any traffic):
- Pin image and model artifact IDs in the rollout config (artifact pin format: model:v2024-11-12-build-ff3a).
- Confirm KMS keys and ensure logs are routed to secure bucket for the cohort.
- Create ephemeral dashboard (copy template: vanguard-template) with these widgets: 95th latency, p95 request queue length, error rate (4xx/5xx split), token-generation time, company-level client error breakdown, model-output quality score (if available).
- Enable verbose KV-cache metrics and cache-miss sampling for the cohort.
- Slack channel: create #vanguard-<release>-<owner> and invite SRE oncall + product owner + client SE.
- Run local smoke: 50 requests through the exact pinned config and compare outputs vs baseline. Save diff artifacts.

Warmup sequence (procedural):
1) Shadow traffic for ~30–60 minutes (no routing) with cold-cache to capture KV load shape.
2) Route 0.05% traffic for 10 minutes (steady-state), watch latency/queue; keep auto-burst disabled.
3) If stable, route 0.25% for 20 minutes and enable request-sampling at 100% for this cohort (collect full responses).
4) If stable, escalate to 1% for 30 minutes, enable automated regression checks.

Gating signals (explicit go/no-go — any one triggers rollback):
- p95 latency exceeds baseline + 250ms for two consecutive windows (5m each).
- Error rate (5xx) increase > 0.5 percentage points and absolute > 1% for cohort.
- Model-quality metric drop (QA eval harness) > 5% on pinned prompt set.
- Any client-level circuit trips (client-visible errors) for same client twice in 10 minutes.
- Any memory OOMs or repeated worker restarts in serving pool.

Rapid pinback procedure (fastest path):
- Run pinback script /ops/pinback.sh --release <id> — this flips router rules to previous pinned artifact and reduces cohort traffic to zero.
- Notify #vanguard channel, SRE oncall, product owner.
- Keep pinned artifact running for at least 2x warmup duration before attempting retry.

Telemetry / logs to capture (samples and retention):
- Full responses for 100% of cohort for first 3 hours, then sample 10%.
- Trace every request with trace-id prefix "vgrd-"; set retention of traces to 30d for followup.
- Store model logits/temperatures diff for failing cases (s3 uri pattern: s3://reinf-vanguard/<release>/diffs/).

Client handoff notes (for partner integration):
- Ask client SE to sign off on specific acceptance prompts (3–5 prompts that represent their heavy use-cases).
- Provide client a short oscilloscope: expected latency range, known tokenization differences if quantization used.
- Offer temporary SDK toggle so client can opt-out if they see regressions.

Open questions / hypotheses to validate in this run:
- Hypothesis A: prefix caching warmup reduces observed p95 by ~15% after 10 minutes — need to verify with cache-miss slice.
- Hypothesis B: new quantized kernel increases tail latency for long-sequence (>1024) requests — validate with sequence-length indexed traces.
- Hypothesis C: some tenants may see different effective temperature due to tokenization drift; store example pairs to spot-check.

Notes from last vanguard (2024-10-29):
- Observed transient p95 spike after 12m due to worker restart; root cause: ephemeral GPU driver handshake on worker that had not been drained properly. Remediation: add worker preflight drain step in pipeline.
- Found one client whose prompt set triggered hallucination regression; rollback done, follow-up patch added prompt-masking.

Small helpers / commands I keep handy:
- curl check: curl -H "x-vanguard: <id>" https://api.reinf.test/generate -d @sample.json | jq '.meta.latency'
- pinback: /ops/pinback.sh --release v2024-10-29-build-ff3a --force
- copy dashboard: dashboards/copy vanguard-template -> vanguard-<release>-<owner>

Post-mortem agenda (if rollback):
- Timeline (with UTC timestamps)
- Who observed first abnormal signal
- Relevant traces and logs (attach s3 diff bundle)
- Action items: immediate (hotfix), short-term (pipeline change), long-term (observability addition)

Personal reminders:
- Keep the rituals short and repeatable — heavy cognitive load during rollouts is the enemy.
- When in doubt, err on the side of safety for tenant-facing cohorts.
- Save at least one “interesting” failing case to the shared repro bucket for model team to iterate.

End of entry.
(Will append with run-specific observations when we execute next vanguard.)
